description:
Trigger: oscal/emit.rs:776-793 (finding_seed), 797-807 (risk_seed), and the similar buf.extend_from_slice patterns in report_seed / subject_seed / EvidenceKey::seed concatenate fields into the UUIDv8 SHA-256 input WITHOUT unambiguous separators between every field. finding_seed places exactly one separator byte (after lint_id) but appends the severity_label byte, detail message, cert_index bytes, and cert_sha256 directly without trailing markers.

Concrete collision shape: two distinct findings can produce the same seed bytes when the bytes appended after the single 0x00 separator can be split in two ways. E.g.:
  finding A: lint_id='foo', severity='e', detail='bar'      → seed = ...|foo|0x00|e|bar
  finding B: lint_id='foo', severity='e', detail='bar' but with a different cert_index that happens to be ASCII bytes equal to the next region → the same byte sequence

Actual bad behavior: distinct findings can in principle collide on UUID. The 122-bit version-8 output gives ~2^61 birthday-bound collision resistance against a brute-force attacker, but an attacker with ANY influence over the detail message (which comes from certificate content via lint message strings — see e.g. ExtendedKeyUsage extension absent from leaf certificate in rfc5280.rs:362) does not need to brute-force the full hash. They only need to collide the seed bytes.

Currently exploitable? No — lint_id values are author-controlled, severity_labels are fixed, and the cert_index + cert_sha256 fields are positionally fixed-width. The realistic worst case is an attacker-crafted certificate whose detail string differs from a benign one but produces the same seed. This requires bit-precise alignment that the current field set makes impractical.

Why P3 (defense-in-depth, not P2): the engineering posture is wrong even though no concrete exploit exists today. Adding a new field to Finding in a future version could remove the positional guarantee that currently saves us. The standard cure is length-prefixed serialization or explicit separators after every variable-length field.

Fix: in finding_seed, risk_seed, and EvidenceKey::seed, prefix every variable-length field with a 4- or 8-byte length tag (u32::to_le_bytes(s.len() as u32)) instead of, or in addition to, the trailing 0x00 separators. Equivalently, hash a tagged structured input: hasher.update(&(f.lint_id.len() as u32).to_le_bytes()); hasher.update(f.lint_id.as_bytes()); ...

Section: G (algorithm and parameter choice — hash input canonicalization)
title: UUIDv8 seed construction in oscal::emit has delimiter-ambiguous field concatenation
